audit_scope: Dan Hallagan / Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core standard 16-space, twelve-turn, 2–4-player multiplayer with base objective deck; all marked expansions and optional variants excluded.

independence.statement: Read only the assigned snapshot and authorized primary/supplemental sources. No question bank, answer key, reader output, grading result, repair note, or previous review/history was read.

conclusion: No material rules error or important omission identified in the assigned scope.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked base/core 2–4-player standard multiplayer, 16 track spaces but twelve turns per player, base objective deck and exclusion of marked expansion/variant rules.

source_evidence.evidence: Core setup is the unmarked standard-length 2–4-player setup. Standard seasons contain three turns and a courtship; hiring when passing is an expansion rule or optional base variant. Objective appendix identifies each included deck explicitly.
Player Aid Note confirms the change in default seasonal market churn and directs play to the compendium page 23 end-of-season order.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked family draft order, baseline and Cavendish reputation, family bonuses, starting servants/tiles/cards/money, leftover starter guests, limited hire supply, monument selection and setup market exclusions/orientation/sorting, open first theme and Fairchild placement.

source_evidence.evidence: Family selection begins left of the first player. Cavendish starts 1.4; York gets a footman; Ponsonby £300; Asquith the Dowager. Supply is one valet and maid and two footmen per player, two underbutlers total. Select player count plus one double-sided monuments with at most one Estate monument. Starting market has six distinct eligible PR≤3 tiles, excludes Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Unused starters return to casual deck.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked exact step sequence, exact attendee type/count, activity and gentry staffing, mandatory favours/positive-before-negative, purchase, cleanup destinations, one-step servant rotation, pass recovery/benefit order, round advancement and standard event locations.

source_evidence.evidence: All players take a turn clockwise; only last player advances marker. Passing first refreshes all service and recovers discarded gentry, then checks events/ongoing effects, then £200 or refresh and optional purchase. Round event precedes ongoing tiles. Every played gentry is discarded, all servants used in any capacity expended; activity tile returns/upgrades.
Original standard-track illustration confirms fairs 3/9, objectives 6, Builders’ Holiday 11, National Holiday 14 and courtships 4/8/12/16.

checked_claim_groups.group: Reputation, screening, special actions and money
checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked five increments per level, 1.1 floor and Max.5 ceiling, fixed screening at end of step 2, later payments, PR acquisition versus play, holiday waiver, special-action costs/repeat limits, public/unlimited money and unaffordable negative favours.

source_evidence.evidence: Special actions: 2 reputation for £100; 3 for one Quarters servant to Available; 4 for Market refresh once per turn. Screening reputation is fixed before step 3. Minimum reputation prevents opponent targeting/special actions. Negative money must be paid, using positive activity favours, borrowing or VP card if needed. At Max.5 special actions may occur even while resolving a reputation favour.

checked_claim_groups.group: Servants, substitutions, hiring and service comparisons
checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked common/unique distinctions, substitution availability conditions, underbutler supply/destination/availability delay, Butler’s Room hiring/recruiting, Butler’s Pantry, Servants’ Quarters improvement versus Service Help versus ordinary rotation and Refresh Service.

source_evidence.evidence: Housekeeper substitutes only without available maids; Brushing Room allows footmen only without available valets. Underbutler may substitute for male base servants even if available and only comes via Pantry, initially Expended. Room hires up to two from supply or, upgraded, recruits one common servant from any opponent-board location. Quarters improvement permits direct use of one Quarters servant; Refresh Service moves all servants straight to Available.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked invite-from-hand versus acquisition-from-deck, kept/rejected screening visibility and destinations, optional dismissal from hand/activity/discard, family immunity, casual respectable/unsavoury classification, all base family and exceptional guest entries, Fairchild sex/type/service/VP and Young Lady bonus.

source_evidence.evidence: Family have no PR/service and cannot be dismissed. Guests acquired via invite are revealed into hand; rejected screened guests return unrevealed to deck bottom. Lord £200; Lady screening or dismissal; Heir £100 or one reputation; Young Lady casual guest plus two reputation for a male prestige attendee; Dowager both £100 and one reputation. Base Charles gives three reputation and Elizabeth gives prestige guest plus two reputation; both Fairchilds are prestige guests without PR and worth eight VP. Base gossips match the listed opponent/self reductions. Marked nonbase entries were excluded.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked all unmarked base tile appendix entries, mandatory first upgrades, hybrids, monument versus category status, ongoing-step timing, Private Study, Barn, Servants’ Hall, service ability tiles, all three suites, Main Library and standard West Terrace. Checked printed requirements and summary deferral to remaining printed tiles for important omitted exceptions.

source_evidence.evidence: Ordinary upgrade is mandatory; hybrids flip each use and only current face-up category counts. Ongoing tiles cannot host. Barn applies when hosting Estate activity. Heritage doubles all guest favours including negatives, Queen’s doubles one chosen favour, Lionheart draws prestige guest without personal service and doubles nonnegative favours before keeping/discarding it. Main Library front grants objective and upgraded side VP card. Standard West Terrace retains three-family/butler activity on both faces; upgraded favour is prestige guest plus optional dismissal of one to four. Private Study upgrades to fair-only £300/two reputation.

checked_claim_groups.group: Market, Reserve, refresh and multiple purchases
checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked price modifiers/floor, no duplicates by any acquisition method, six-space refill and duplicate stacks, partial/multiple-space sorting, Reserve qualification/visibility/prices, Largest Wine Cellar exclusion, refresh removal/refill/return order, seasonal refresh and unchanged-market purchase timing.

source_evidence.evidence: Buy one total normally, £300 Reserve price plus modifier and £100 floor. Reserve takes Service after first season (except Wine Cellar), PR1 after second, and qualifying later draws immediately. All Reserve tiles public and purchasable. Refresh sets aside only Market, refills all six spaces, then returns removed tiles to bag. Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase allow any number with no sliding/refill or refresh between purchases; complete purchases before refill. Special-action refresh cap is distinct from pass benefit and multiple VP refresh cards.
Seasonal Flowchart player aid is incomplete because it omits the now-default new-season market refresh.

checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked initial/drawn/discarded/retained objective counts, bottom-deck destinations and simultaneous shuffle, extra retained objective effects, every base-deck group/guest/category/servant/tile/reputation/monument/wealth objective, and all VP card benefits/use windows/destinations.

source_evidence.evidence: Base objectives: five setup plus two round-event, one discard at each courtship, three retained absent extra objectives. Owning tiles suffices, upgrades unnecessary. Base group names/tile sets/VP and all base bonuses match. Category bonuses include monuments/current hybrids; basic servants are only valet/maid/footman. VP Objective draws two/keeps one; Refresh Guest returns one gentry including family; Hire Servant excludes underbutler and goes Expended; used VP cards go deck bottom and cannot also score.

source_evidence.source: Official French publisher base rulebook (restricted clarification only)
source_evidence.evidence: Page 7 identifies Max as level 7 in standard play. Page 14 objective example states the maximum reputation level is attained as indicated by the Max counter. This supports the unchanged seven-VP reputation objective at level 7 independently of wheel position; no French gameplay flow used.

checked_claim_groups.group: Courtship, seasonal upkeep, final scoring and ties
checked_claim_groups.checked: Checked ordinary and final theme scoring including negative tiles/repeated categories/current hybrids, reward/tie rules, Fairchild return and final retention, objective discard, anticlockwise first-player movement, final action window, all seven score sources and courtship/game tie hierarchy.

source_evidence.evidence: Courtship contains no turns/rotation/monument income/Hall. First three courtships compare current theme, ties draw VP and no Fairchild. Upkeep is Reserve → full refresh → reveal theme → first player anticlockwise → advance. Final courtship uses all four themes; reputation level, ignoring wheel position, breaks theme ties. Final actions/VP benefits allowed before scoring. Final scoring includes all face-up tile VP, all owned hand/discard gentry VP, remaining objectives, triangular level score through 28, two VP per servant, floor(money/200), unused VP cards. Game ties use final Fairchild, reputation level, shared victory.

original_pdf_visual_checks.details: Inspected original-PDF rendered illustrations for standard round-track events, Queen’s Suite category/monument transition, South Lawn requirements, base objective groups/deck labels and reputation/monument objective imagery; French page 14 checked only for Max-counter objective clarification. French page 7 read as primary PDF text for standard Max=7.
